name: Finding patterns and anomalies in networks
gist: Papers focused on detecting unusual nodes or patterns in graphs, clustering similar items together, and understanding what makes certain nodes or subgraphs stand out.
explain: Sometimes the question is not 'predict a label for each node' but 'what is unusual?' In a fraud-detection network, most transactions are legitimate, but a few follow suspicious patterns. In a sensor network, most readings are normal, but a few nodes are failing. In a recommendation system, most user-product pairs are unrelated, but a few clusters of users want the same things. Detecting these unusual things—anomalies—is different from typical classification: you need to find what deviates from normal, and normal is often defined by patterns in the network itself.

This is hard because anomalies are rare, so you don't have many examples to learn from. Also, what counts as anomalous depends on context. A sudden traffic spike is suspicious in an email network but normal in a shopping network. And some anomalies hide by mimicking normal patterns. An adversary committing fraud may deliberately try to look like normal users around them.

Papers here develop techniques to identify subgraphs and clusters that stand out—groups of nodes that are tightly connected to each other but loosely connected to everyone else. They use outlier detection on graph embeddings (vector representations of nodes), looking for nodes whose position in the learned space is far from their neighbors. They study which subgraphs appear frequently versus rarely. Some use multi-view clustering: the same nodes may form different clusters depending on which type of edge you focus on, and anomalies stand out in some views but not others.

papers.title: A Consensus Anchor-guided Hypergraph Framework for Incomplete Multi-view Clustering
papers.contribution: Achieves superior clustering accuracy and maintains high efficiency even in scenarios with severe data incompleteness, validated across diverse benchmarks.

papers.title: Compactness and Consistency: A Conjoint Framework for Deep Graph Clustering
papers.contribution: CoCo outperforms state-of-the-art counterparts on various benchmark datasets for deep graph clustering.

papers.title: Contractive Anchor Resolvent Diffusion for Incomplete Multi-View Clustering
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive performance while scaling linearly in N for fixed anchor budget, without explicit view imputation, across eight benchmarks including large-scale datasets.

papers.title: Diverse and Sparse Mixture-of-Experts for Causal Subgraph–Based Out-of-Distribution Graph Learning
papers.contribution: The framework achieves strong performance on the GOOD benchmark across synthetic and real-world structural shifts by modeling instance-level heterogeneity through diverse, sparse expert selection.

papers.title: Federated Graph-Level Clustering Network with Dual Knowledge Separation
papers.contribution: FGCN-DKS demonstrates superiority over state-of-the-art methods on multiple graph benchmark datasets.

papers.title: GraphFLEx: Unsupervised Structure Learning $\underline{\text{F}}$ramework for $\underline{\text{L}}$arge $\underline{\text{Ex}}$panding $\un
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on 26 diverse datasets with significantly improved scalability, demonstrated across different GNN architectures.

papers.title: Hierarchical Anchor Graph Learning for Multi-View Clustering
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets and provides a scalable, trustworthy paradigm for hierarchical knowledge representation in broad machine learning tasks.

papers.title: Normality Calibration in Semi-supervised Graph Anomaly Detection
papers.contribution: GraphNC consistently and substantially enhances performance of teacher models from different GAD methods and achieves new state-of-the-art performance.

papers.title: Constant Degree Matrix-Driven Incomplete Multi-View Clustering via Connectivity-Structure and Embedding Tensor Learning
papers.contribution: Reduces computational complexity from O(n²) to O(1) while eliminating post-processing, achieving better clustering performance through coordinated optimization of graph connectivity and high-order correlations.

papers.title: Deep Multi-view Graph Clustering via Attribute-aware Bidirectional Structural Refinement and Pseudo-label Guided Multi-level Fusion
papers.contribution: Superior clustering performance on six homophilic and heterophilic datasets through bidirectional graph refinement and multi-level fusion guided by reliable pseudo-labels.

papers.title: Discretely-Refined Multi-view Clustering via Aligned Anchor Learning
papers.contribution: DRMC refines graph structure through discrete feedback and exhibits significant advantages over existing methods on multiple benchmarks.

papers.title: Discriminative Attribute Graph Clustering Through Topology-Guided Contrastive Learning
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms six state-of-the-art baselines on four widely-used graph datasets (ACM, DBLP, CITE, AMAP) through topology reconstruction and mutual information minimization.

papers.title: Edge-colored Clustering in Hypergraphs: A MaxECC Approximation
papers.contribution: Improves best-known approximation factor for all hypergraphs; for graphs achieves 0.43 factor versus previous 0.38.

papers.title: Escaping the Homophily Trap: A Threshold-free Graph Outlier Detection Framework via Clustering-guided Edge Reweighting
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance by dismantling the homophily trap and eliminating the need for predefined anomaly thresholds.

papers.title: FSD-CAP: Fractional Subgraph Diffusion with Class-Aware Propagation for Graph Feature Imputation
papers.contribution: We propose FSD-CAP, a two-stage framework designed to improve imputation quality under extreme sparsity

papers.title: FedRGL: Robust Federated Graph Learning under Label Noise
papers.contribution: Achieves 5-8% higher accuracy on average and up to 30% improvement over weaker baselines under various noise conditions across real-world graph datasets.

papers.title: Fully Dynamic Coreset Spectral Clustering
papers.contribution: Achieves the best known trade-off between query time and update time for the Normalised Cut problem, with practical performance improvements over state-of-the-art on real-world datasets.

papers.title: Learning Discriminative and Generalizable Anomaly Detector for Dynamic Graph with Limited Supervision
papers.contribution: Demonstrates superiority across diverse evaluation settings in learning discriminative and generalizable anomaly detectors.

papers.title: MCbiF: Measuring Topological Autocorrelation in Multiscale Clusterings via 2-Parameter Persistent Homology
papers.contribution: MCbiF Hilbert functions provide interpretable topological features for machine learning tasks, outperforming baselines on regression and classification of non-hierarchical partition sequences.

papers.title: MDGMIX: Boundary-Aware Subgraph Mixing for Multi-Domain Graph Pre-Training
papers.contribution: MDGMIX consistently outperforms baselines in few-shot classification while exhibiting superior time and memory efficiency, reducing redundancy in multi-domain graph pre-training.

papers.title: Neural Graduated Assignment for Maximum Common Edge Subgraphs
papers.contribution: Significantly improves computation time and scalability on large instances while enhancing performance on MCES, similarity estimation, and graph retrieval tasks.

papers.title: OPTION: Optimal Transport–Guided Flow Matching for Incomplete and Unaligned Multi-View Clustering
papers.contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods across ideal, incomplete, and unaligned scenarios with optional contrastive regularization for aligned settings.

papers.title: OWLEYE: ZERO-SHOT LEARNER FOR CROSSDOMAIN GRAPH DATA ANOMALY DETECTION
papers.contribution: Enables zero-shot graph anomaly detection across unseen domains without retraining, with continuous and scaling-up learning capabilities.

papers.title: Rethinking Feature Alignment in Generalist Graph Anomaly Detection: A Relational Fingerprint-based Approach
papers.contribution: REFI-GAD significantly outperforms state-of-the-art across 14 datasets through semantic-aware feature alignment and domain-specific adaptation.

papers.title: Topological Anomaly Quantification for Semi-supervised Graph Anomaly Detection
papers.contribution: Demonstrates superiority over state-of-the-art methods through topological quantification and effective anomaly enhancement on benchmark datasets.

papers.title: Towards Anomaly-Aware Pre-Training and Fine-Tuning for Graph Anomaly Detection
papers.contribution: APF achieves superior performance on 10 benchmark datasets and theoretically achieves linear separability under mild conditions.
